Implemented `python/ray/llm/_internal/common/placement.py` with two Pydantic models.

**`BundleConfig`** — `CPU`/`GPU` fields defaulting to `0.0`, with `extra="allow"` so arbitrary named resources (e.g. `TPU`) are accepted. A `mode="before"` model validator runs every value (declared and extra) through `_coerce_resource_value`, which:
- rejects non-numeric values (and `bool`) with a `"must be a number"` message,
- coerces ints/fractionals to `float`, so `model_dump()` always emits floats,
- rejects negatives with a `"non-negative"` message.

**`PlacementGroupConfig`** — `bundles: Optional[List[BundleConfig]]`, `bundle_per_worker: Optional[BundleConfig]` (raw dicts are auto-coerced to `BundleConfig` by Pydantic, so `.CPU`/`.GPU` are accessible), and required `strategy`. A `field_validator` checks `strategy` against the canonical `VALID_PLACEMENT_GROUP_STRATEGIES` from `ray.util.placement_group` (raising a Pydantic `ValidationError`). A `mode="after"` validator enforces exactly-one-of with the `"either 'bundle_per_worker'"` and `"Cannot specify both"` messages — these are `ValueError`s, and since `pydantic.ValidationError` subclasses `ValueError`, `pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...)` catches them. `model_dump()` drops the unused `None` bundle field so output contains only the provided key plus `strategy`.

All twelve behavioral requirements verified end-to-end. No test files were touched.
